content: The page lists three possible pairs of primitive relations for an atelier structure, then describes the earlier choice of ≤ and the curved subdivision order. It presents ≪ as the generated preorder and gives G ≪ F iff there exists F′ with G ≤ F′ curved-order F.

The author says the geometric/intuitive center of gravity lies in subdivision, but describes the technical burden of deriving properties of ≪ and proposes instead to begin with ≤ and ≪. The alternative using ≪ and compatibility is called a curiosity.

A right note rejects the sufficiency of the opening alternatives under a new point of view. The oblique note says the point of view will change on page 20: the curved order is to be determined from ≪ and ≤, instead of ≪ being determined as above.
